title: Tag Link Management Delivery
summary: narrow New Tag preflight, migrate tags to canonical public document URLs, and deliver shared published-document search plus Tag Registry link management
content_html:
Tag Link Management Delivery

Target Result

Tag Registry stores an ordered array of optional one-way canonical document locations for each tag. Tag Registry and Edit Tag present current document titles, Edit Tag can search published document titles and add a selected location through a reusable picker or remove an association, and the registry no longer stores or presents a tag description. Tag Editor searches published Analysis locations only. Shared results retain report context, while Tag Registry's compact title-only rows suppress it; scope context appears only for consumers configured with more than one scope.

The relationship and independent-lifecycle boundary remains owned by Tag-document linking.

As a prerequisite, New Tag stopped auditing every existing registry association. Its job remains one atomic result: validate the submitted tag, allocate and create one fresh Analysis tags document, append the new linked registry row, rebuild the child projection, and report the outcome. The later schema cutover records that freshly created canonical location at doc_url[0].

Status And Order

Current state: TLM-0 through TLM-5 are complete. The shipped behavior and remaining weak spots are reconciled into the durable Tag Registry, Tag Source Data, and Tag-document linking documents.

Review rule: TLM-1 records an already accepted planning decision, not shipped behavior. Complete implementation checkpoints TLM-0 and TLM-2 through TLM-5 in order, record evidence beneath each checkpoint, and stop for review before starting the next.

Frozen Data Contract

The next registry schema uses doc_url as an ordered array of canonical same-origin Docs Viewer locations:

{
  "doc_url": [
    "/analysis/?doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=d-20260727-225608-63967a",
    "/docs/?scope=studio&doc=d-20260729-151446-09489e"
  ]
}
  • doc_url: [] means the tag is not linked. New Tag writes its newly created Analysis tags location at index 0; later picker selections append in commit order.
  • The URL is the association identity because it preserves the chosen report context. The same source document may therefore appear more than once through different canonical report URLs.
  • The same canonical URL cannot occur twice within one tag, but any number of tags may reference it. Add and remove operations identify the complete URL rather than relying on a mutable array index.
  • A canonical URL is a normalized repository-relative viewer route produced by Docs ownership. It includes the configured viewer base and scope behavior, the exact report-host document where applicable, and the exact displayed document. It excludes fragments, transient filters, and arbitrary query state unless a later contract deliberately makes them part of location identity.
  • It never stores a scheme or host. The same root-relative value resolves against the local origin while working locally and the public origin after publication.
  • Each scope uses its configured canonical viewer base. Analysis locations use /analysis/?doc=<report-doc-id>&subdoc=<document-id>; they do not store a local /docs/?scope=analysis... alternative. A scope whose canonical base is /docs/ still uses that configured route.
  • Tag Registry UI can add only a URL returned by the supported document-location provider; it exposes no free-form URL or ID input. The write API validates the complete array's supported canonical shape and duplicates, but does not recheck current provider membership because a selected location may become unavailable before confirmation.
  • Stale URLs remain stored, visible, and removable. No title match, selected parent, displayed document, or alternative report may silently replace them.

The registry does not store document or report titles. A shared document-location provider resolves each stored URL to current presentation data such as {url, scope_id, document_title, report_title, available}. Picker results represent actual report placements, not just documents: the same source document may appear as separate choices such as bird-nerve — All Tags and bird-nerve — Made-up Tags.

The provider searches public projections, not management or source collections. Its initial coverage is published Analysis and Library documents plus their configured published sub-scopes. The picker adapter requires a non-empty consumer-supplied scopeIds allowlist and has no implicit all-supported-scopes default. Tag Editor supplies ["analysis"]. The provider loads and returns only records from the requested supported scopes. Top-level public search records and sub-scope placement records contribute one searchable result per canonical URL. Hidden, manage-only, local-only, and unpublished documents are absent, so every new selection has a public route that also resolves against the local origin during local work.

Provider records always retain scope_id. A picker configured with one scope omits the redundant scope label; a picker configured with more than one shows it. Report context remains visible when present because distinct report placements can have distinct canonical URLs. Scope-label visibility follows the configured allowlist length, not the scopes represented by the current query results. Consumers may suppress report context in their presentation without removing it from the committed record; Tag Registry does so while duplicate visible titles remain uncommon.

The picker commits one reusable result such as {url, scope_id, document_title, report_title}. Consumer adapters determine how it is written:

  • Tag Registry stores url in doc_url[] and renders it as a title link in the Registry table.
  • Ordinary document authoring inserts url as the destination of a Markdown link.
  • A future document-capable Semantic Token adapter uses url as the generated target-lookup href; Semantic Token source continues to store its registered token identity rather than embedding a raw URL in token syntax.

These are three uses of the same selected canonical URL, not three picker or route contracts. Plain-link and Semantic Token authoring remain later consumers; this delivery proves the shared result through Tag Registry first.

Frozen Interaction Contract

  • Edit Tag shows doc_url[] as title-only pills in array order. Each pill title links to its exact configured public-preview location; identical visible titles need no extra disambiguation.
  • The picker is permanently visible with scopeIds: ["analysis"]. It searches published Analysis titles in a fixed four-result scrolling viewport and omits redundant scope and report context. Selecting a result fills the search field and enables the adjacent +; + appends that exact URL to the draft. The placeholder explains the field without a separate visible label; the input retains an accessible label. Results use the input font size, with a paler pointer hover than the committed selection highlight.
  • The picker excludes an exact URL already present in the draft. A different URL with the same document title remains a valid result.
  • Each pill owns a direct × removal action. It changes only the modal draft; it does not navigate, delete the document, or mutate canonical data.
  • Edit Tag Save writes the complete revised doc_url[] with the other accepted tag edits in one atomic registry mutation. Cancel discards all draft additions and removals. A successful save closes without echoing the backend audit summary into the page; errors and warnings remain visible.
  • A URL that no longer resolves is shown as Unavailable document, remains linked to its exact stored location, and can be removed. The stored URL is not repaired or replaced.
  • The Tag Registry table replaces description with documents. It renders document titles as comma-separated links in doc_url[] order and renders — for an empty array. Equal titles remain equal; no report label is added. Local hrefs resolve against Studio's configured public-preview base.
  • Pill × is deliberately distinct from Tag or document deletion.

This is the current TLM-4 review contract. Ordinary-width and narrow-width fit, tactile selection behavior, and final wording are decided against the working UI.

The schema cutover retires the tag-row description field. This does not alter alias descriptions or the independent contents of existing linked documents.

TLM-0 Prerequisite Contract

Before TLM-0, the creation planner called registry_document_ids, which validated the complete registry as though New Tag owned association integrity. It rejected creation when any existing row had a missing, duplicate, non-immutable, or non-resolving doc_id.

That is wider than the creation responsibility:

submitted New Tag
  -> validate new tag_id, scalar group, and description
  -> reject an existing tag_id
  -> allocate one fresh document identity
  -> create one new document and linked row atomically
  -> rebuild the exact Analysis/tags projection

existing registry associations
  -> preserve unchanged
  -> do not audit or repair during New Tag

TLM-0 is deliberately limited to that current-schema prerequisite. description removal and doc_url[] creation start after its review gate.

New Tag retains the guards required for its own write:

  • require the supported registry version and a registry tags array;
  • validate the submitted fields and reject an existing tag_id;
  • resolve the configured direct-child document root and confine the new path;
  • allocate the immutable ID directly from the document timestamp and cryptographic token, without supplying registry or source identities; and
  • preserve the existing atomic Registry/document write, targeted rebuild, compensation, activity, response, and manual-patch contracts.

The planner does not inspect any existing registry doc_id, inventory document IDs for allocation, compare the generated ID with registry rows, or preflight the destination's existence. write_text_atomic_new is the sole collision boundary: it refuses to overwrite a real destination if the generated identity does collide. That create-only write is filesystem safety, not registry association validation. Focused association audit and repair belong to the later link-management workflow.

Delivery Tracker

[x] TLM-0 — Narrow New Tag To Its Own Write

  • [x] Remove registry_document_ids and all other existing-association reads from document-ID allocation and row creation.
  • [x] Stop inventorying Analysis document IDs or checking destination existence before the exclusive-create write.
  • [x] Keep validation of the new tag, new row, new immutable document ID, configured source root, confined path, and atomic create-only destination.
  • [x] Prove creation succeeds while unrelated existing rows include:
    • no doc_id;
    • a shared doc_id;
    • a stale doc_id; and
    • a malformed doc_id.
  • [x] Preserve duplicate-new-tag_id, invalid submitted field, destination collision at exclusive create, write/rebuild failure, compensation, response, activity, and manual-patch behavior.
  • [x] Remove helpers and tests whose only purpose was whole-registry or whole-collection document-ID preflight.
  • [x] Run focused creation/planner/API tests and the narrow maintained Tag Registry smoke boundary.
  • [x] Record exact tested and untested surfaces and inspect the final diff.

Checkpoint / review gate: New Tag creates one correct linked tag/document pair without certifying unrelated associations. No links UI, association mutation, repair, or presentation change starts before user review.

Ready for review. Stop here before TLM-2.

TLM-0 Evidence

  • New Tag now validates the supported v4 container and submitted row, resolves the configured Analysis tags source root, allocates directly from the new document timestamp and cryptographic token, and plans only the new row and confined destination. It no longer reads existing registry associations or inventories Analysis documents.
  • Focused creation proves a successful commit while unrelated rows are unlinked, share one resolving doc_id, hold a stale immutable doc_id, and hold a malformed legacy value. Focused row creation also permits a shared doc_id while retaining duplicate-new-tag_id and submitted-field guards.
  • Destination existence is not checked during planning. The atomic write_text_atomic_new call is the collision boundary and preserves an existing destination byte-for-byte. Registry-byte revision checking, Registry/document compensation, targeted child rebuild, response, and activity paths are unchanged.
  • Focused Python evidence passed 22 tests across test_tag_document_creation.py, test_tag_registry_mutations.py, and test_studio_tag_workflows.py. This covers planning, real child projection, exclusive-create collision, Registry-write and rebuild compensation, dry-run/API response, invalid input, and retry evidence.
  • A write-free plan against the current canonical v4 Registry produced one confined, absent destination and left the Registry byte-for-byte unchanged.
  • Maintained studio-tag-smoke passed all 11 checks, including the fixture create API, linked source, targeted rebuild, response/activity boundary, and route modules. Run evidence: var/admin/test-runs/tag-link-management-tlm0-localhost/summary.md. The first sandboxed run could not bind its fixture servers to 127.0.0.1; its ten failures were environment failures, and the localhost-permitted rerun is the product evidence.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for the four changed implementation/test files, and git diff --check passed. The final source and generated diff were inspected after rebuilding this delivery document.
  • No live canonical tag or Analysis document was written. Manual patch source and UI modules were unchanged and covered only by maintained source/module checks, not a direct fallback interaction. No links UI, schema v5 migration, association mutation, repair, provider/picker, browser interaction, or ordinary/narrow visual review was attempted.

[x] TLM-1 — Freeze The Cutover And Interaction

  • [x] Use one-way tag_registry_v4 to tag_registry_v5 migration with no dual-schema compatibility path.
  • [x] Support published Analysis and Library documents plus their configured published sub-scopes behind a required consumer scope allowlist; Tag Editor requests Analysis only. Exclude Studio, manage-only, local-only, hidden, and unpublished documents.
  • [x] Use one shared title-search picker whose records retain scope/report context and commit one canonical URL plus presentation data. Omit scope from one-scope presentation while retaining report context.
  • [x] Keep the Edit Tag linked-document list title-only and permit equal titles.
  • [x] Use adjacent picker + and direct pill × draft actions, then commit the complete URL array only on Edit Tag confirmation.
  • [x] Replace the registry description column with comma-separated document title links and an empty-state dash.
  • [x] Keep stale URLs visible as Unavailable document and removable without repair.

Checkpoint accepted: the persistence, search, modal, table, and downstream consumer contracts are frozen. Visual and tactile acceptance waits for the working UI.

[x] TLM-2 — Cut Over The Registry And New Tag

Start only after TLM-0 is accepted.

  • [x] Add tag_registry_v5 validation for ordered canonical doc_url arrays.
  • [x] Migrate each nonblank v4 scalar to its current canonical Analysis tags report URL; migrate a missing or blank scalar to [].
  • [x] Remove tag-row description during the same guarded migration while preserving row order, tag_id, scalar group, timestamps, policy, aliases, assignments, documents, and document content.
  • [x] Reject noncanonical, unsupported, external, and within-tag duplicate new URLs without rejecting shared URLs across different tags.
  • [x] Remove description from New Tag input, validation, registry writes, direct API and manual-patch contracts. A new document starts from its tag title without a duplicated registry description.
  • [x] Record the freshly created Analysis tags canonical URL at doc_url[0] without reading existing URL arrays for uniqueness or stale-link checks.
  • [x] Preserve TLM-0's exclusive-create collision boundary, atomic registry and document write, rebuild, compensation, activity, and failure behavior.
  • [x] Remove v4-only readers and writers after the migration; do not retain a compatibility alias or silent scalar/URL normalization in the live app.
  • [x] Reconcile the canonical migration and run focused schema, migration, creation, API, rollback, and manual-patch evidence.

Checkpoint / review gate: canonical v5 data and New Tag are accepted before association mutation or browser picker integration.

Checkpoint accepted.

TLM-2 Evidence

  • The one-way migration replaced all 246 nonblank v4 doc_id scalars with /analysis/?doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=<doc-id> at doc_url[0]. It removed all 246 tag-row descriptions and scalar IDs while preserving ordered tag_id, scalar group, row timestamp, and policy values. The migration also covers blank or missing legacy IDs as []; the applied input contained none.
  • Registry reconciliation reports 246 ordered rows and 246 document URLs. Aliases remain 70 entries with 71 targets, assignments remain eight references, their source fingerprints remain 9bdcd5ac7df75719ba791480ff45612137ce1832e5c0595eaf8e23a376701158 and 08c0dba8bf923be376f1b8186290a00b1a2bdb7c74ad811f896eb1f430b72d5d, and no Analysis tags document source changed.
  • Live Registry loading now requires tag_registry_v5 and exact row fields. Ordered arrays accept supported canonical Analysis, Library, and configured local Docs routes. Validation rejects external, fragment-bearing, unsupported, malformed, and within-row duplicate URLs while permitting the same exact URL on different tags. Historical v1-to-v4, label-retirement, and document-bootstrap utilities remain explicitly pinned one-time tools rather than live v4 compatibility.
  • Docs Viewer owns canonical sub-scope location generation from configured viewer base/scope behavior and the exact report-host source. Migration, first-class New Tag creation, Studio runtime config, and manual patch output consume that owner. A new tag appends its fresh URL without inspecting other rows' URL arrays.
  • New Tag no longer renders, validates, sends, stores, or manually patches a description. Direct creation rejects a supplied description. Its new Analysis source contains front matter plus # <tag-id> only.
  • The existing exclusive-create destination guard, revision check, atomic Registry/document write, exact child rebuild, compensation, activity, and response behavior remain covered. Focused schema/migration/mutation tests also cover empty arrays, shared cross-tag URLs, invalid URLs, rollback, and real sub-scope projection.
  • All 287 Studio Python tests passed with an isolated writable catalogue media base. Maintained studio-tag-smoke passed all 11 checks, including Studio source lint, fixture APIs, actual route readiness, New Tag input retirement, manual-patch modules, linked-source creation, rebuild, compensation-adjacent boundaries, and activity. Run evidence: var/admin/test-runs/tag-link-management-tlm2-final-4-localhost/summary.md. The immediately preceding sandboxed attempt allowed source lint but blocked all ten localhost fixtures; the localhost-permitted rerun is the product evidence.
  • git diff --check passed and the final canonical migration was validated by the same command in read-only mode. No TLM-3 provider/picker, link add/remove, or association mutation was implemented. The existing Edit Tag description and Registry-table presentation are deliberately left for TLM-4, so no realistic link-management or narrow-width visual review was attempted.

[x] TLM-3 — Deliver The Shared Document Location Provider And Picker

  • [x] Add the reusable local-authoring document-location picker under shared/frontend/, using the existing shared search-list behavior rather than creating another listbox implementation.
  • [x] Keep the picker independent of a route shell so Tag Registry and later local authoring consumers can provide their own adapters.
  • [x] Require each consumer to supply a non-empty scopeIds allowlist. Keep supported-collection policy, durable form state, and writes with the consuming app; keep the low-level shared search-list record-only. The picker passes the allowlist to the provider and commits one exact canonical URL plus presentation data; it does not serialize Tag Registry values, Markdown links, or Semantic Tokens itself.
  • [x] Add a compact public document-location search projection and provider for published Analysis and Library documents plus their published sub-scopes. Load and return only requested supported scopes, fail closed for empty or unsupported scope requests, and emit one canonical root-relative URL per actual placement with its document, scope, and report presentation data.
  • [x] Build from public search/index and sub-scope placement ownership only. Do not read manage manifests, local published workspaces, source front matter, or local Docs APIs in the picker.
  • [x] Permit one source document to appear in several provider records when distinct report-host documents surface it. Do not construct a report/document cross-product or assume one report host per sub-scope.
  • [x] Search document titles case-insensitively as the user types, rank exact and prefix matches ahead of other title matches, and preserve distinct placements with duplicate titles.
  • [x] Support asynchronous loading, keyboard/pointer commit, empty results, and provider failure. Retain scope on every record; show it only when scopeIds.length > 1. Show report context when present. Do not vary scope-label visibility from the current result set.
  • [x] Exclude exact URLs already attached to the edited tag from selectable results while preserving them in the existing-link list.
  • [x] Add pure component/provider, public-projection, and exact route/module wiring evidence.

Checkpoint / review gate: approve provider results and picker behavior before allowing the picker to mutate Tag Registry.

Checkpoint accepted. TLM-4 started only after user approval and the accepted TLM-3 work was committed.

TLM-3 Evidence

  • Docs Viewer now owns deterministic docs_document_locations_v1 projections beside the public Analysis and Library search indexes. Records contain only canonical URL, scope ID, document title, and report title; they are derived from public search records, public report payloads, and the matching public sub-scope manifest. Source documents, manage manifests, and local APIs are outside the builder.
  • The checked-in public projections contain 250 Analysis locations: two top-level documents and 248 currently published Concepts placements. The Library projection contains 14 top-level locations. The TLM-2-created bird-nerve source remains absent because its public sub-scope projection has not been published; TLM-3 did not publish or otherwise promote that document.
  • Publication confirm/apply now includes the location projection for supported scopes, using the exact parent, search, and sub-scope bytes eligible for the same publication. The standalone builder exists only to reconcile the projection from the already published site/ artifact and is idempotent for both current scopes.
  • The shared provider requires a non-empty Analysis/Library scopeIds allowlist, fetches only those per-scope indexes, validates schemas and canonical URLs, caches successful scope loads, and fails closed for malformed or unsupported data. Title search is case-insensitive with exact, prefix, then containing-match rank while retaining equal-title report placements.
  • The shared picker adapts the existing search-list primitive and returns only {url, scope_id, document_title, report_title}. It supports dynamic exact-URL exclusions, keyboard and pointer commit, empty and failure states, report context, and scope context based on configured allowlist length. The generic search list now ignores stale asynchronous responses after later input, close, commit, or teardown, and cannot commit an earlier match while a newer request is pending.
  • Focused Python evidence passed 41 tests across the location builder, publish gate, builder bootstrap, Studio asset/runtime route, and Admin target map/config boundaries. After final review narrowed publication inputs to actually placed public sub-scopes, the affected builder/publish slice passed all 10 tests. Explicit Python and JavaScript source lint passed, as did the complete maintained shared and docs-viewer lint scopes. The projection-contract audit passed, both generated indexes rebuilt to an unchanged result, and git diff --check passed.
  • The focused Playwright module smoke loaded the real Analysis and Library projections through Studio-compatible routes, then proved requested-scope loading, ranking, duplicate placements, exact exclusion, stale resolution, one- and multi-scope presentation, keyboard and pointer commit, empty and failure states, invalid commit rejection, and stale asynchronous response suppression.
  • Maintained studio-tag-smoke passed all 11 checks, including the complete Studio source lint boundary, fixture tag APIs, local routes, the real provider/picker module and data paths, and retained Tag Editor readiness. Run evidence: var/admin/test-runs/tag-link-management-tlm3-final-7-localhost/summary.md.
  • TLM-4 remains intentionally absent: the picker is not mounted in Edit Tag, no Registry URL draft is displayed or changed, no description/table presentation was altered, and no ordinary- or narrow-width Tag Registry visual review was attempted.

[x] TLM-4 — Integrate Tag Link Management

  • [x] Add focused atomic append/remove operations using explicit tag_id plus the complete draft doc_url[]; confirmation changes only the associations and accepted tag fields and never deletes a document.
  • [x] Preserve unrelated tag rows, URL order, aliases, assignments, documents, and document content.
  • [x] Replace the Tag Registry description heading, cells, and sort projection with documents, rendering current titles as comma-separated links in URL order and — for no links.
  • [x] Remove tag-description controls and state from New Tag and Edit Tag.
  • [x] Render zero, one, or many title-only linked-document pills in Edit Tag. Equal titles remain unchanged, each title links to its exact public-preview location, and each pill has a direct remove action.
  • [x] Keep the shared picker permanently visible with scopeIds: ["analysis"], a fixed four-result scrolling viewport, and title-only results. The adjacent + appends the result selected into the search field.
  • [x] Use each pill's × to remove that exact URL from the draft without deleting a document.
  • [x] Commit the complete URL draft atomically on Edit Tag confirmation and discard it on cancel.
  • [x] Render an unresolved URL as Unavailable document in both surfaces while keeping its Registry-table and Edit Tag links and making its pill removable.
  • [x] Never expose free-form ID or URL entry in Tag Registry UI and never infer a location from the displayed document, selected tree row, title, group, or an alternative route.
  • [x] Add focused planner, API, atomic-write, activity, failure, retry, frontend-domain, and route-module evidence before realistic UI review.
  • [x] Review realistic linked, unlinked, multi-link, shared, duplicate-title, multi-report, search-no-match, provider-failure, and stale examples at ordinary and narrow widths.

Checkpoint / review gate: user acceptance of the actual title list, picker, remove interaction, and state language before closeout.

Ready for review. Stop here before TLM-5.

TLM-4 Evidence

  • Edit Tag now owns a complete ordered doc_url[] draft. + accepts only an exact Analysis record committed by the shared provider; pill × drops that exact URL; Close discards the draft; Save sends the complete array with immutable tag_id and the accepted group.
  • The mutation API requires and validates that complete canonical, duplicate-free array, writes the registry through the existing atomic transaction, and reports exact added/removed counts. It deliberately does not require current provider membership: a previously valid location may become unavailable before confirmation and remains a supported removable stale association.
  • Tag Registry and Edit Tag resolve current titles from the public location projections. Both retain stored URL order and exact URL identity, show Unavailable document for unresolved URLs, and no longer carry canonical tag-description controls or presentation. Registry-table hrefs resolve against Studio's configured public-preview base instead of the Studio server.
  • Edit Tag uses linked-title document pills with direct × removal. Its permanent title-only picker keeps a fixed four-row scrolling viewport; a selected result fills the search field and the adjacent + adds only that provider record. The + is drawn as centered strokes rather than relying on a font glyph's baseline.
  • Focused planner, route, activity, workflow, and runtime tests passed 37 checks. Explicit changed-source Python and JavaScript lint passed. The local Registry API smoke proved a two-link ordered edit, added/removed counts, unrelated-source preservation, and the existing create/delete lifecycle. The route test also forced one atomic-write failure, verified unchanged source bytes, and passed the same complete request on retry.
  • The focused browser module smoke passed provider success/failure, stale fallback, equal titles with exact identities, shared and multiple URLs, Analysis-only append, exact removal, cancellation, ordered request payloads, no-change/reorder behavior, permanent-picker selection, title-only result presentation, linked-title pills, and public-preview href construction.
  • In the live Tag Registry, ordinary- and 390-pixel-width review covered the document column, half-width Edit Tag modal, permanent fixed-height results, scrolling beyond four rows, no-match stability, title-only results, search-adjacent + placement, linked pill titles, direct pill × removal, draft cancellation, and narrow fit without horizontal overflow. The picker has no redundant visible label; result and input text are both 14 pixels, result rows are about 32 pixels high, four rows remain fully visible, pointer hover is paler than selection, and + is geometrically centered. Its desktop width was 416 pixels; at a 390-pixel viewport it was 358 pixels wide by 484 pixels high. A Registry link opened the configured port-4000 public Analysis preview. No browser errors were present.

[x] TLM-5 — Integration And Closeout

  • [x] Run the accumulated focused service, API, route-module, and maintained Tag Registry checks chosen by the accepted interaction.
  • [x] Verify migration, optional, ordered, shared, stale, duplicate-title, multi-report, and standalone-document behavior without implying synchronization or exclusive ownership.
  • [x] Inspect the final source and generated diff independently.
  • [x] Move only stable shipped behavior and remaining weak spots into Tag Registry and Tag Source Data.
  • [x] Close or split any unapproved follow-on rather than widening this delivery.

TLM-5 Evidence

  • Seventy-five focused Python tests passed across the v5 source model and migration, Registry mutation/API/activity, New Tag creation, Studio runtime and workflow, document-location builder, Docs build CLI, and publication gate. This re-ran the service and projection seams accumulated across the accepted checkpoints.
  • Maintained studio-tag-smoke passed all 11 checks: Studio source lint, Registry/Alias/Assignment/Promotion API fixtures, local tag routes and groups, series rendering, Tag Registry route/provider/picker modules, and neighboring ready states. Run evidence: var/admin/test-runs/tag-link-management-tlm5-closeout/summary.md.
  • The current canonical Registry passed read-only v5 reconciliation with 247 tags, 246 document URLs, 70 aliases/71 targets, and eight assignment references. It contains one valid unlinked row and no within-row duplicate URLs. That unlinked row came from the concurrent accepted UI edit and was preserved, not introduced as a closeout fixture.
  • Migration/schema tests prove populated and empty v4 scalar cutover, description retirement, preserved order, supported route validation, within-row duplicate rejection, and cross-tag sharing. Mutation/API tests prove ordered complete-array replacement, optional empty arrays, unrelated row preservation, exact add/remove counts, atomic failure preservation, and retry.
  • The maintained route-module smoke proves resolving and stale presentation, duplicate visible titles with distinct exact URLs, two report placements for one source document, exact exclusion/add/remove, public-preview hrefs, provider failure, and the absence of a route-level verbose success echo. Document-location projection tests prove both actual report placements and standalone top-level records while excluding source/manage-only data.
  • The projection-contract audit passed. Rebuilding both checked-in public document-location indexes was idempotent: Analysis remained 250 records and Library 14.
  • Final source and generated diffs were inspected after the durable-doc rebuild. The three durable documents now own current UI, v5 write/schema, and independent-lifecycle behavior; their by-ID payloads, tree status, recent list, and search timestamps contain the corresponding generated changes. Generated JSON parses cleanly and git diff --check passes.
  • Automatic stale repair, bulk mutation, drag reorder, Library/Studio picker authoring, second-consumer integration, and Tag semantic tokens remain explicit follow-ons. General Studio documentation sorting is also separate; none was started by this closeout.

In Scope

  • Removing complete-registry association validation from New Tag.
  • Relying on generated identity plus the atomic exclusive-create write, without registry or document-inventory uniqueness preflight.
  • Evidence-led discovery of the actual link-management UI need.
  • An ordered doc_url array of canonical cross-scope document locations.
  • A guarded v4-to-v5 migration and tag-description retirement.
  • Live document and report-title resolution without registry title duplication.
  • One reusable, provider-driven published-document location picker with a required consumer scope allowlist.
  • Provider coverage over public Analysis, Library, and published sub-scope projections, with Analysis-only title search in Tag Editor.
  • Edit Tag title-only listing plus draft exact-URL append and remove.
  • Tag Registry comma-separated document-title links.
  • Optional, multiple, shared, resolving, stale, and unlinked relationship states.

Not In Scope

  • Synchronizing tag group with document content or metadata.
  • Making tags own document deletion or documents own tag deletion.
  • Inferring, deduplicating, or automatically repairing associations.
  • Reordering document URLs.
  • Editing document titles or content from Tag Registry.
  • Bulk link mutation.
  • Automatically supporting every configured Docs scope or sub-scope.
  • An implicit all-supported-scopes picker mode.
  • Persisting fragments, temporary filters, or other incidental viewer state.
  • Searching source, manage-only, hidden, local-only, or unpublished documents.
  • Adding authoring controls to the live public site.
  • Integrating the picker into a second local authoring workflow in this delivery.
  • Redesigning the Analysis Concepts collection or generic sub-scope report.
  • Tag semantic-token implementation.
  • Renaming tag_id, adding a Concept identity model, or changing alias and assignment semantics.

Starting Authority

  • creation planner and transaction: studio/services/tags/tag_document_creation.py
  • focused row creation: studio/services/tags/tag_registry_mutations.py
  • API boundary: studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/registry.py
  • current Tag Registry route and modules: studio/app/frontend/routes/tag-registry.html and studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-*
  • current local search-list interaction reference: shared/frontend/js/search-list.js
  • public scope configuration, search, sub-scope manifests, and canonical route projection: site/docs-viewer/config/defaults/docs-viewer-public-config.json, site/assets/data/search/, site/assets/data/docs/scopes/, site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-configured-scope-provider.js, and docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/sub_scope.py

These are inspection starting points. The picker remains local, app-neutral authoring behavior; Tag transport and mutation remain Studio-owned, while its search inputs, public placement data, and canonical URLs remain Docs Viewer-owned.

Completion Gate

Complete only when the New Tag prerequisite is independently accepted, the v5 migration and description retirement are reconciled, the shared provider and picker have a real Tag Registry consumer, the exact inspect/add/remove workflow is shipped and realistically reviewed, and durable owners describe the resulting current behavior without turning URL order or bootstrap output into ownership or one-to-one relationship invariants.
